rationale: 9 blocking findings: 3 critical AC failures (total count never rendered, object attributes still JSON.stringify'd, metadata failures unrecoverable via Retry because it shares the listEvents error field) plus 6 major defects (two request races in the modal, unencoded projectName in the request path, an over-broad currency-key regex, a dropped entity_type-only label, and actor_id silently dropped from the migrated detail view). No lens failed and none appears in lens_truncated; standards audit found no blocking issues and no coverage gap. 1 pre-existing item deferred (ActivityEventsPage's Event column bypasses the new label helper, unchanged since before this diff). 8 additional lens-reported items dismissed: two are explicitly authorized by spec.md (History-button gating on !isPersonalProject only, and the fixed Budget/Members/Settings category list), the rest were speculative or verified as non-issues (test-file automock scoped safely, forceRerender comment, null-to-undefined coercion, malformed-date edge case, and the row-expansion affordance, which already has a proven dedicated Expand column).

findings.title: Total matching count is never displayed
findings.problem: Pagination preserves filters correctly, but the API's total matching count has no rendering path: ProjectActivityHistoryModal passes pagination.totalCount into Table's pagination prop, Table.tsx only reads totalCount to compute isLazyMode (which additionally requires onSelectAllChange, never passed here), and PaginationProps/Pagination.tsx has no total-count field or rendering at all — it only ever shows page numbers.
findings.impact: The required acceptance criterion "displays the total matching count from the API" has no implementing UI anywhere in the diff; a project admin can never see how many total events match their filters.
findings.recommendation: Add a total-count prop to Pagination (or render it directly beside the Table in the modal) and wire pagination.totalCount into it.

findings.title: actor_id dropped from migrated detail view
findings.problem: The pre-migration Popup rendered a "Actor ID" DetailRow whenever selectedEvent.actor_id was present. The new toPresentable() mapping (used by both renderEntity/renderActor and renderExpandedRow via getEventAttributeRows) omits actor_id entirely, and PresentableActivityEvent's shape does not carry it either.
findings.impact: actor_id, a previously-visible audit identifier, is no longer shown anywhere in the UI after this migration.
findings.recommendation: Surface actor_id in the expanded row (or the Actor cell) when present, e.g. by including it in the presentable shape or appending it to getEventAttributeRows' output.

findings.title: No sequencing guards overlapping listEvents/loadMetadata calls
findings.problem: loadEvents and the mount-time loadMetadata call fire with no AbortController or request-id tracking; changing filters quickly can fire overlapping listEvents calls.
findings.impact: A slower earlier response can resolve after a newer one and overwrite the store with stale events/pagination for a filter the user has already changed away from.
findings.recommendation: Track a request id (or AbortController) per call and ignore a response that is not the latest before writing it into the store.

findings.title: Page-size change races the filter effect back to page 0
findings.problem: onPaginationChange calls setPerPage(limit) and loadEvents(page, limit) directly, but perPage is also a dependency of the filter-driven useEffect (line 142-145) that calls loadEvents(0, perPage) whenever perPage changes.
findings.impact: Changing the page size triggers a second, conflicting load that resets back to page 0 right after (or racing with) the explicit page-preserving load, so the user's requested page is silently discarded.
findings.recommendation: Exclude perPage-only changes from the filter effect (e.g. split it into a filters-effect and a perPage-effect, or gate the effect with a ref to skip the redundant reload).

findings.title: projectName not URL-encoded in the request path
findings.problem: projectName is interpolated directly into `v1/projects/${projectName}/activity-events...` (and the metadata endpoint at line 83) with no encodeURIComponent, unlike every other v1/projects/${...} call in the codebase (projects.ts, projectDisplayNames.ts).
findings.impact: A project name containing '/', '?', '#', or spaces would corrupt the request path or query string.
findings.recommendation: Wrap projectName with encodeURIComponent at both call sites, matching the existing codebase convention.

findings.title: Metadata failures cannot be recovered via Retry
findings.problem: listEvents and loadMetadata both write failures into the same shared `error` field; listEvents clears it on entry but loadMetadata does not. The modal's handleRetry only re-issues store.listEvents.
findings.impact: A metadata-endpoint failure surfaces the generic error/Retry UI, but clicking Retry can never re-issue loadMetadata, so recording_enabled stays unresolved indefinitely after a metadata-only failure — violating the required retry-recovers acceptance criterion.
findings.recommendation: Use separate error fields (eventsError/metadataError) and have handleRetry re-issue whichever call actually failed.

findings.title: AMOUNT_KEY_HINT regex over-matches non-monetary keys
findings.problem: AMOUNT_KEY_HINT = /(amount|budget|spend|limit|cost)/i is broad enough to match unrelated numeric keys such as retry_limit or cost_center_id.
findings.impact: A non-monetary numeric attribute whose key happens to contain one of these substrings is formatted as currency, misrepresenting its value in the expanded row.
findings.recommendation: Tighten the hint to whole-word/suffix matches on the specific attribute keys the backend actually emits for budget events.

findings.title: getEventTargetLabel drops entity_type when entity_id is absent
findings.problem: getEventTargetLabel has no branch for an event with entity_type set but no entity_id/entity_label; it falls through to '—', whereas the pre-migration renderEntity showed the entity type alone in that case.
findings.impact: An event with only entity_type set renders an em dash instead of the available type information, a regression from the previous rendering.
findings.recommendation: Add `if (event.entity_type) return event.entity_type` before the final fallback.

findings.title: formatAttributeValue still dumps raw JSON for objects
findings.problem: formatAttributeValue falls back to JSON.stringify(value) for any object-typed attribute value; only primitive values are guaranteed a readable rendering.
findings.impact: A nested-object attribute on an event still renders as a raw JSON string inside the expanded row, directly contradicting the required 'never raw JSON' acceptance criterion.
findings.recommendation: Recurse into object values to render named key/value pairs (reusing getEventAttributeRows' own formatting) instead of JSON.stringify.
